name: Retatrutide

b.x: 25.0% mean body weight lost at 80 weeks on 12 mg in TRIUMPH-1 (n=2,339, NEJM 2026) [9], vs 3.9% on placebo. That peer-reviewed analysis counts everyone randomized, including people who stopped the drug, so it runs lower than on-treatment toplines. The smaller TRIUMPH-4 trial (n=445, December 2025) enrolled adults with obesity and knee osteoarthritis. Its Lilly topline reported 28.7% at 68 weeks and has not been peer-reviewed. No head-to-head trial against tirzepatide or semaglutide exists yet. The retatrutide peptide (LY3437943, CAS 2381089-83-2) is a 39-amino-acid synthetic lipopeptide developed by Eli Lilly. Known in community forums as reta peptide or Triple G, it activates GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors simultaneously in a single molecule. The GLP-1 component suppresses appetite and slows gastric emptying. GIP improves insulin response and buffers GLP-1 tolerability. Glucagon raises resting energy expenditure and burns liver fat directly. That third receptor is the differentiator; dual agonists like tirzepatide lack it entirely. Clinicians and researchers tracking the obesity pharmacotherapy space have been watching retatrutide since the Phase 2 readout (Jastreboff et al., NEJM 2023) [1], where 338 adults lost up to 24.2% body weight at 48 weeks on the 12 mg dose. A substudy of that trial in 98 adults with MASLD (Nature Medicine 2024) [2] tracked liver fat. On 12 mg, it fell 82.4% from baseline by week 24. More Phase 3 results landed in 2026. In adults with type 2 diabetes, TRIUMPH-2 (n=1,152) found 18.8% weight loss on 12 mg vs 5.1% on placebo at 80 weeks (Lancet 2026) [13]. TRIUMPH-3, in adults with established cardiovascular disease, reported 22.6% in a Lilly topline (July 2026). Community interest runs highest among people who plateaued on semaglutide or tirzepatide. The enthusiasm is high; so are the GI side effects during dose escalation. Lilly plans to submit a Biologics License Application (BLA) to the FDA in Q1 2027. Until approval, retatrutide carries no FDA approval and no insurance coverage.

Three receptors. One molecule. Retatrutide binds GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors simultaneously, making it the only triagonist in late-stage clinical development. GLP-1 receptor activation suppresses appetite centrally through hypothalamic satiety pathways and slows gastric emptying peripherally. This is the same mechanism behind semaglutide and liraglutide. GIP receptor agonism potentiates glucose-dependent insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells while improving tolerability of GLP-1 effects on the gut. Tirzepatide uses GLP-1 plus GIP; retatrutide adds a third target. The glucagon receptor component is what makes this molecule different. Glucagon activation increases resting energy expenditure and promotes hepatic fat oxidation, converting liver triglycerides to ketone bodies. Phase 2a MASLD data [2] confirmed this clinically: 82.4% relative liver fat reduction at 12 mg in 24 weeks. Comparisons with GLP-1 or dual-agonist liver data are cross-trial only. The triple mechanism produces additive weight loss because each receptor targets a distinct metabolic pathway. Appetite drops. Energy expenditure rises. Liver fat burns off. The result, based on Jastreboff's Phase 2 [1] and TRIUMPH-4 Phase 3 data, is weight loss larger than single or dual agonists produced in their own trials, though no head-to-head trial exists yet.
Retatrutide benefits center on superior weight loss, liver fat clearance, and broad metabolic improvement driven by its triple-receptor mechanism.

Metabolic markers improve across the board: non-HDL cholesterol, triglycerides, hsCRP and systolic blood pressure all fell in TRIUMPH-4, with systolic pressure down 14.0 mmHg on 12 mg (Lilly topline, December 2025).

Aligned
Scientific Evidence
Based on 23 key studies · phase-3
TRIUMPH-1 (NEJM 2026, n=2,339) reported 25.0% mean body weight reduction at 80 weeks on 12 mg, counting everyone randomized.

Dosing studied: 1 mg to 12 mg weekly SC. Phase 3 titration (TRIUMPH-1): start at 2 mg, then 4, 6, 9, and 12 mg, escalating every 4 weeks until the 4, 9, or 12 mg target. Phase 2 (NEJM 2023, PMID 37366315) tested 1, 4, 8, and 12 mg; escalated arms started at 2 or 4 mg, and the 1 mg arm stayed fixed.

TRIUMPH-4's Lilly topline (Dec 2025) gave 28.7% at 68 weeks under the efficacy estimand, or 23.7% counting everyone. Phase 2 demonstrated 24.2% at 48 weeks [1]. MASLD Phase 2a showed up to 82.4% liver fat reduction at 24 weeks [2]. Evidence base is strong across Phase 2 and four Phase 3 obesity readouts (TRIUMPH-1 to -4); TRIUMPH-1 and TRIUMPH-2 are now peer-reviewed.
Key Study

TRIUMPH-4 Phase 3 (Lilly press release, Dec 11 2025): n=445 adults with obesity + knee OA; 12 mg = −28.7% body weight, 9 mg = −26.4% at 68 weeks. Phase 2 obesity (Jastreboff et al., NEJM 2023, PMID 37366315): n=338, −24.2% at 48 wk (12 mg). MASLD Phase 2a (Nature Medicine 2024, PMID 38858523): n=98, −82.4% relative liver fat at 24 wk (12 mg).
Limitations

Not yet FDA approved; Lilly plans a BLA submission in Q1 2027. Phase 3 readouts so far: TRIUMPH-4 (Dec 2025); TRIUMPH-1 (NEJM 2026, PMID 42814954, n=2,339: 17.6%, 23.7%, and 25.0% at 80 weeks on 4, 9, and 12 mg vs 3.9% on placebo under the treatment-regimen estimand; Lilly's May 2026 topline gave 19.0%, 25.9%, and 28.3% vs 2.2% under the efficacy estimand, which assumes everyone stayed on drug; a Lilly-reported extension reached 30.3% at 104 weeks on 12 mg in adults with BMI 35 or higher); TRIUMPH-2 (Lancet 2026, PMID 42810372, n=1,152: 11.9%, 16.8%, and 18.8% vs 5.1% at 80 weeks, treatment-regimen estimand); TRIUMPH-3 (Lilly topline, Jul 23 2026, 22.6% at 80 weeks); TRANSCEND-T2D-1 in type 2 diabetes (Lancet 2026, PMID 42250575). TRIUMPH-3 and TRIUMPH-4 are still Lilly toplines, not yet peer-reviewed. No cardiovascular outcomes trial data yet. Dose-dependent resting heart rate increase observed in Phase 2, peaking at week 24; Phase 3 heart rate data are not yet published. Long-term data beyond 104 weeks absent. Weight regain on discontinuation expected (GLP-1 class effect).
Community Experience
Referred to as "Godzilla" and "Triple G" in weight-loss communities.
Community dosing: 1 mg/week start, titrating to 4–8 mg maintenance for most users. Some push to 12 mg. Community often stretches titration steps to 6–8 weeks per step to manage GI side effects.

High enthusiasm from users who plateaued on semaglutide or tirzepatide. Compounded versions widely used despite investigational status. Stronger and faster appetite suppression than class peers reported, but GI side effects and heart rate elevations are the primary complaints.

Science & Community Aligned

Community titration closely mirrors Phase 2 trial design. Efficacy expectations align with clinical data. Community awareness of heart rate and GI side effects matches Phase 2 safety signals. Community caution about product quality is appropriate given non-approved status.

Clinical Trial Phase 2 trial (NEJM 2023): 1 mg was the fixed low-dose arm. Phase 3 TRIUMPH titration starts at 2 mg; a 1 mg start is community practice [Source](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37366315/)

Phase 3 TRIUMPH trials start retatrutide at 2 mg weekly and step up every 4 weeks. Many community users start lower, at 1 mg (the dose of the fixed low-dose arm in Phase 2), regardless of prior GLP-1 experience. The triple-receptor mechanism means your gut is adapting to three agonists at once. Even users who tolerated tirzepatide at high doses report rougher GI onboarding with retatrutide. Reconstitution math for common vial sizes: a 10 mg vial with 2 mL bacteriostatic water gives you 5 mg/mL. At that concentration, 1 mg equals 0.2 mL, which is 20 units on a standard 100-unit insulin syringe. A 4 mg dose would be 80 units. For the 12 mg maintenance dose, you'll want a 15 mg vial with 2 mL BAC water (7.5 mg/mL); 12 mg then equals 1.6 mL or 160 units. At 160 units, consider splitting across two injection sites to reduce volume discomfort. Track your resting heart rate from day one. The glucagon component raises energy expenditure, and HR is the clearest early signal of dose-dependent cardiovascular stress. If your resting pulse sits above 90 bpm for more than a week, hold the current dose before escalating. Evening injections let you sleep through peak nausea, which typically hits 4 to 8 hours post-injection.
Retatrutide Continuous

Retatrutide is not FDA approved and lacks long-term safety data beyond 104 weeks. Cycling decisions are primarily driven by the need for periodic safety evaluation (heart rate, metabolic markers, liver function) rather than established receptor desensitization. Weight regain on discontinuation is a consistent GLP-1 class effect: continuous use appears necessary for sustained weight maintenance, consistent with its positioning as a chronic disease therapy.

Clean the top of your lyophilized retatrutide vial with an alcohol swab. Draw 2 mL of bacteriostatic water into a syringe and inject it slowly down the inner wall of the vial. Do not shake. Swirl gently until the powder dissolves completely.

Calculate your syringe units With a 10 mg vial and 2 mL BAC water, your concentration is 5 mg/mL. For a 1 mg dose, draw 20 units on a 100-unit insulin syringe. For 2 mg, draw 40 units. For 4 mg, draw 80 units. For 8 mg, draw 160 units (or use a 15 mg vial at 7.5 mg/mL for higher doses; 8 mg then equals approximately 107 units).
Pinch a fold of skin at your injection site (abdomen, outer thigh, or upper arm). Insert a 29 to 31 gauge needle at a 45 to 90 degree angle. Inject slowly. Hold for 5 seconds before withdrawing.
Rotate injection sites Never inject the same quadrant within two weeks. Abdomen is preferred for absorption consistency.
Inject once weekly on the same day Evening dosing is preferred so peak nausea (4 to 8 hours post-injection) occurs during sleep.
Store the reconstituted vial refrigerated at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius. Use within 4 weeks.
Works With
BPC-157

Gastroprotective properties documented in preclinical models. Community widely co-uses BPC-157 to mitigate GI side effects (nausea, gastric discomfort) during retatrutide titration. No clinical trial combination data exists.
250–500 mcg SC or oral daily, particularly during the first 4–12 weeks of retatrutide titration
Avoid
Semaglutide

Both agents activate GLP-1 receptors. Combining GLP-1 agonists stacks GI side effects (nausea, vomiting, gastroparesis) with no incremental efficacy benefit: retatrutide's GLP-1 component already provides full GLP-1 agonism.
Tirzepatide
Tirzepatide is a GLP-1/GIP dual agonist. Combining with retatrutide creates redundant GLP-1 and GIP receptor activation with compounding GI risk and no clinical rationale.
CagriSema (cagrilintide + semaglutide)
Adding a fixed-dose GLP-1 combination on top of a triple GLP-1/GIP/glucagon agonist introduces overlapping GLP-1 activity and entirely unstudied additive risk.
Insulin / Sulfonylureas
Retatrutide's GLP-1 and GIP components both lower blood glucose; combining with insulin or sulfonylureas increases hypoglycemia risk, especially in type 2 diabetes. Medical supervision required.

Gastrointestinal events during dose escalation are the defining tolerability challenge with retatrutide. Community users often describe them as rougher than on other GLP-1 drugs, though no head-to-head trial has tested that. In TRIUMPH-4 Phase 3 data (Lilly topline 2025), nausea occurred in 38 to 43% of participants. Diarrhea affected 33 to 35%. Constipation hit 22 to 25%. Vomiting was reported in 21%. Side effects led 12.2% on 9 mg and 18.2% on 12 mg to stop, vs 4.0% on placebo. These rates are dose-dependent and front-loaded, meaning they peak during the weeks immediately after each dose increase. Most GI events resolve within 1 to 2 weeks at a stable dose. Stepping up slowly, with 4 weeks between escalations as the Phase 3 trials do, is the standard way to limit them. Raised resting heart rate is the second signal that deserves attention. Phase 2 trials [1] documented a dose-dependent increase in resting HR tied to glucagon receptor activation. Community users at 8 mg and above have reported palpitations and sustained HR above 90 bpm. The TRIUMPH-1 and TRIUMPH-2 abstracts report no heart rate figures, so anyone with a cardiac history should track heart rate weekly during titration. Do not escalate if resting HR stays above 100 bpm. Dysesthesia is the newer Phase 3 signal. It means abnormal skin sensations such as tingling, burning, or numbness. In TRIUMPH-4 it showed up in 8.8% on 9 mg and 20.9% on 12 mg, vs 0.7% on placebo. TRIUMPH-1 reported 5.1 to 12.5% across the 4, 9, and 12 mg doses, vs 0.9% on placebo. Most cases were mild to moderate and resolved during treatment (Lilly topline figures; the TRIUMPH-1 NEJM abstract does not give dysesthesia rates). TRIUMPH-2 (Lancet 2026) [13], in 1,152 adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes, flagged low blood pressure. Hypotension hit 1%, 5%, and 6% on 4, 9, and 12 mg vs under 1% on placebo. Dysesthesia ran 4 to 7% vs 1%. Gastrointestinal events were still the most frequent: diarrhea hit 27 to 34% vs 13% on placebo, and nausea 14 to 28% vs 8%. Stopping for side effects or death ran 12% on 9 mg and 8% on 12 mg, vs 4% on 4 mg and 5% on placebo. Lightheadedness on standing is worth a blood pressure check. Post-injection fatigue, sometimes called "wipeout day," shows up consistently in community reports at doses of 8 mg or higher. Users describe pronounced fatigue lasting 12 to 24 hours after injection, particularly during the first 2 to 4 weeks at a new dose level. Scheduling the injection on a low-demand day helps. The GLP-1 class carries an unresolved rodent thyroid C-cell tumor signal. No confirmed human thyroid cancer risk has been established for any GLP-1 agonist, but retatrutide is contraindicated in anyone with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN2). Pancreatitis is a known class risk. Severe persistent abdominal pain radiating to the back warrants immediate medical attention and discontinuation. Pregnancy is an absolute contraindication. No human pregnancy data have been published for retatrutide. Discontinue well before any planned pregnancy. Product quality adds a layer of risk specific to investigational peptides. Retatrutide is not FDA approved; compounded versions lack standardized formulation. A Certificate of Analysis with HPLC purity data is the only check on each batch. Grey-market research chemicals carry contamination and identity risks that cannot be verified.
Common Issues & Solutions

Severe nausea 1–3 days post-injection: Extend current dose step to 6–8 weeks before escalating. Inject in the evening so peak nausea occurs during sleep. Anti-nausea medications (ondansetron, promethazine) are routinely used in clinical practice. Some community users add BPC-157 daily during titration.

Resting heart rate elevated (>90–100 bpm): Dose-dependent glucagon receptor effect seen in Phase 2. Do not escalate dose until HR normalizes. If persistent at current dose, step down one level. Avoid stimulants (caffeine, pre-workout). HR should normalize within weeks at a stable dose.

Weight loss stalling at low doses (1–2 mg): Usually incomplete titration, not a plateau: 1–2 mg are tolerability steps, not therapeutic targets. Escalate per protocol if GI symptoms allow. Stalls at therapeutic dose (8–12 mg) may reflect a new metabolic equilibrium.

Injection site reaction (redness, nodule, bruising): Normal subcutaneous response. Rotate strictly between abdomen, thigh, and upper arm quadrants: never inject the same quadrant within 2 weeks. Warm the reconstituted vial briefly in your hands before injecting.

Fatigue and "wipeout" the day after injection (at ≥8 mg): Reported in community at higher doses, particularly in the first weeks at a new dose level. Schedule injection on a low-demand day. Ensure hydration and electrolyte replacement: GI fluid losses compound fatigue. Typically resolves within 2–4 weeks at a stable dose.

Retatrutide (LY3437943) is an investigational drug. It has not received FDA approval for any indication. Eli Lilly reported Phase 3 results from TRIUMPH-4 (December 2025), TRIUMPH-1 (May 2026), and TRIUMPH-2 and TRIUMPH-3 (July 2026). Lilly plans to submit a Biologics License Application (BLA) to the FDA in Q1 2027. Outside clinical trials, Lilly runs a pre-approval expanded access program (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07629401, first posted June 5, 2026, status Available). It is open to adults who can't join a retatrutide trial and have a BMI of 35 or higher despite the highest available dose of weight management therapy. They also need two or more serious obesity-related complications. Retatrutide does not appear in FDA's 503A bulk substance categories (updated May 14, 2026), and no FDA-approved retatrutide product exists. FDA warning letters dated September 9, 2025 say drugs compounded with retatrutide are not eligible for the 503A or 503B exemptions. Products sold as compounded retatrutide are not the investigational drug used in Lilly's trials, and no regulator has checked their purity or dose. For athletes subject to anti-doping testing, WADA's 2026 Prohibited List does not name retatrutide or any other GLP-1 receptor agonist. Retatrutide has no regulatory approval, though, so it may fall under section S0 (non-approved substances), which WADA prohibits in and out of competition. Check with your anti-doping organization before use. All content on this page is for educational and informational purposes only. It does not constitute medical advice. Consult a licensed healthcare provider before using any investigational compound.

phases.timing: Same day each week; evening preferred to sleep through peak nausea
phases.notes: GI adaptation phase. Side effects peak here as body adjusts to triple-receptor activation. Do not escalate early even if well-tolerated: allow gut time to adapt.

phases.notes: TRIUMPH-4 Phase 3 dose: 28.7% mean weight loss at 68 weeks. Not all users require or tolerate 12 mg: 9 mg showed 26.4% and may offer better tolerability.

protocols.monitoringNotes: Check resting heart rate weekly during titration. Lipid panel and liver enzymes at baseline and 12 weeks. Blood glucose monitoring if diabetic or pre-diabetic.

protocols.goal: Weight loss: slow community titration for GI-sensitive users

phases.name: Micro-initiation
phases.syringeUnits: 10 units (10 mg vial + 2 mL BAC water → 5 mg/mL)
phases.notes: Community-derived sub-trial starting dose for highly GI-sensitive individuals. No clinical trial data at 0.5 mg. Efficacy at this dose is minimal; purpose is GI adaptation only.

phases.name: Step 1
phases.syringeUnits: 20 units (10 mg vial + 2 mL BAC water → 5 mg/mL)

phases.name: Step 2
phases.syringeUnits: 40 units (10 mg vial + 2 mL BAC water → 5 mg/mL)
phases.notes: Meaningful appetite suppression and early weight loss at this step. Some GI-sensitive users find this a sustainable long-term dose.

phases.name: Maintenance
phases.syringeUnits: 80 units (10 mg vial + 2 mL BAC water → 5 mg/mL)
phases.notes: Community consensus maintenance for conservative protocol. Good efficacy with lower GI burden vs. 8–12 mg. No clinical trial data on this specific slow titration schedule.

protocols.duration: Ongoing; no defined cycle endpoint in community protocols
protocols.monitoringNotes: Track resting heart rate weekly. Note GI symptoms and extend current dose step if needed before escalating.

phases.name: Standard titration (same as obesity protocol)
phases.syringeUnits: Per weight-loss protocol above (20 → 40 → 80 → 160 units with 10 mg vial + 2 mL BAC water)
phases.notes: Community schedule mirrors the weight-loss protocol above. In the Phase 2a MASLD trial (PMID 38858523), liver fat reduction was dose-dependent and tracked closely with weight loss.

phases.name: MASLD maintenance
phases.syringeUnits: 160 units at 8 mg (10 mg vial + 2 mL BAC water); 160 units at 12 mg (15 mg vial + 2 mL BAC water → 7.5 mg/mL)
phases.notes: Phase 2a: −81.4% liver fat at 8 mg and −82.4% at 12 mg at 24 weeks. 79–86% of participants achieved normal liver fat (<5%). Liver fat benefit appears to plateau between 8–12 mg.

protocols.duration: 48 weeks (Phase 2a duration); Phase 3 weight-maintenance trial TRIUMPH-6 (NCT06859268) ongoing
protocols.monitoringNotes: Liver fat quantification via MRI-PDFF or CAP at baseline and 24 weeks. ALT/AST every 3 months. FibroScan or liver biopsy per hepatologist guidance if fibrosis staging is required.

faqs.q: How much weight can you lose on retatrutide?
faqs.a: In TRIUMPH-1 (n=2,339), mean body weight fell 17.6%, 23.7%, and 25.0% at 80 weeks on 4, 9, and 12 mg, vs 3.9% on placebo (NEJM 2026, PMID 42814954). Those peer-reviewed figures count everyone randomized. Lilly's earlier 28.3% topline estimated the effect if everyone had stayed on the drug. The smaller TRIUMPH-4 trial (n=445) reported 28.7% at 68 weeks on 12 mg, a company topline that has not been peer-reviewed. In separate trials, tirzepatide reached 20.9% (SURMOUNT-1) and semaglutide 14.9% (STEP 1); no head-to-head study exists. Results depend on dose titration speed and adherence to the escalation schedule.

faqs.q: What are the most common retatrutide side effects?
faqs.a: Nausea affected roughly 38 to 43% of participants in Phase 3 TRIUMPH-4, with diarrhea near 33% and vomiting near 21%. Most GI symptoms peak during dose escalation and taper as the body adjusts. Phase 2 data also showed a dose-dependent resting heart rate increase that peaked around week 24. Phase 3 added dysesthesia (tingling, burning, or numb skin): 8.8 to 20.9% on retatrutide vs 0.7% on placebo in TRIUMPH-4, and 5.1 to 12.5% vs 0.9% in TRIUMPH-1. Most cases were mild to moderate.

Not yet. Eli Lilly plans to submit a Biologics License Application (BLA) to the FDA in Q1 2027, after the TRIUMPH-1 to -4 Phase 3 readouts (Lilly, July 23 2026). Lilly says it is first finishing the manufacturing (CMC) data package the application needs (July 23, 2026 release).

faqs.q: How does retatrutide differ from tirzepatide?
faqs.a: Tirzepatide is a dual agonist (GIP + GLP-1). Retatrutide adds a third target: the glucagon receptor. That glucagon activity drives additional energy expenditure and hepatic fat reduction. Phase 2 data showed a 24.2% weight loss vs tirzepatide's 20.9% in separate trials, though no head-to-head study exists.

faqs.q: What is the retatrutide dosing schedule?
faqs.a: Phase 3 trials (TRIUMPH-1) start at 2 mg weekly and step up every 4 weeks: 2, 4, 6, 9, then 12 mg. The 4 mg target takes one step; reaching 12 mg takes 16 weeks of escalation. Phase 2 (NEJM 2023, PMID 37366315) started escalated arms at 2 or 4 mg and kept one arm fixed at 1 mg. Many community users start at 1 mg and hold each step longer to limit nausea. Skipping steps increases GI side effects without improving long-term outcomes.

faqs.q: How many mg is 20 units of retatrutide?
faqs.a: It depends on the vial. This assumes 2 mL of bacteriostatic water and a 100-unit insulin syringe, where 20 units is 0.2 mL. A 5 mg vial gives 2.5 mg/mL, so 20 units is 0.5 mg and 1 mg is 40 units. A 10 mg vial gives 5 mg/mL, so 20 units is 1 mg. A 15 mg vial gives 7.5 mg/mL, so 20 units is 1.5 mg and 1 mg is about 13.3 units. Always check the vial size and water volume before drawing.

Retatrutide rates a B on the Peptide Schedule safety scale, and its two biggest flags are dose-dependent gastrointestinal effects and a resting heart rate increase tied to glucagon receptor activation. Phase 3 TRIUMPH-4 reported nausea in roughly 43% of participants at the 12 mg dose, with the heart rate rise peaking around week 24. It has no FDA approval yet, so product quality from compounded or grey-market sources stays a real variable.
Retatrutide typically comes in 5mg or 10mg or 15mg vials. Add 2mL of bacteriostatic water to the vial. Use the free calculator for exact syringe units based on your desired dose.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of Retatrutide?
faqs.a: The half-life of Retatrutide is ~6 days. This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.
